record.statement: Determine the subcritical linear-variance and critical/supercritical subvolume-variance regimes for particle counts in windows of the free-chain torus configuration.
record.statement_caveat: The literal source permits every box with size-uniform constants. That lower bound fails for boxes filling almost the whole torus. The intended mesoscopic or bounded-volume-fraction regime remains open.
record.status_search: Focused searches on 2026-09-07 for ARW density, cutoff, local limits, hyperuniformity and incompressibility; four later primary papers read at stated theorem scope. No certificate of present openness.
record.title: Onset of mesoscopic hyperuniformity in the ARW free chain

record.independent_check: On a cycle, S_B=k-I_x for the omitted site x. Therefore Var(S_B)=Var(I_x)<=1/4 exactly. Translation invariance from uniform driving even gives Var(I_x)=(k/L)*(1-k/L).
record.method: Conservation, explicit coupling reduction, exact law comparison or spectral calculation
record.obstruction: This is a scope counterexample to the unrestricted window quantifier. It does not settle variance growth for windows small compared with the torus, nor the critical exponent.
record.result: At step k the free chain has exactly k sleeping particles on N=L^d sites. Thus Var(S_B)=Var(S_Bc) and Var(S_B)<=min(|B|,N-|B|)^2/4. Taking the proper box B=[0,L-2] times the full other d-1 coordinate intervals leaves only L^(d-1) sites outside B. In d=1, B has L-1 sites and Var(S_B)<=1/4, contradicting a size-uniform lower bound c*(L-1) at any fixed positive subcritical density. The contradiction does not depend on a simulation or the full-torus endpoint.
